subject: science
notes: Fast radio bursts are flashes of radio waves that last only a few thousandths of a second.
The first was identified in 2007, in data that a radio telescope had recorded in 2001.
Most bursts come from galaxies far beyond our own, which has made their sources hard to identify.
Astronomers proposed many possible sources, including magnetars, the dense, highly magnetic remains of dead stars.
In April 2020, telescopes detected a fast radio burst coming from a known magnetar in our own galaxy.
It was the first time a fast radio burst had been traced to a known object.
stem: The student wants to present the 2020 detection as evidence for one proposed explanation of fast radio bursts. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Magnetars had been proposed as one possible source of fast radio bursts, and in 2020 a burst was detected coming from a known magnetar in our galaxy.
choices.B: In April 2020, for the first time, telescopes traced a fast radio burst to a known object, a finding that came thirteen years after the first burst was identified.
choices.C: The first fast radio burst was identified in 2007, in data that a radio telescope had recorded six years earlier, in 2001.
choices.D: Because most fast radio bursts come from galaxies far beyond our own, astronomers have found it hard to identify their sources and have proposed many possibilities.

explanation.why: To present the detection as evidence for an explanation, the sentence must name the explanation (magnetars as a proposed source) and show that the 2020 burst came from a magnetar. Only one choice links the observation to the hypothesis it supports.
explanation.A: Correct. It names magnetars as a proposed source and reports a burst traced to a known magnetar, so the detection reads as evidence for that idea.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It reports the 2020 detection but never says what kind of object produced the burst or which explanation it supports. This is the most attractive near miss because it stresses that the detection was a first.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It gives the history of the first detection, not the 2020 evidence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It explains why the sources were hard to identify but does not mention the 2020 detection.
